title: Microsoft Teams: two presenters can share screens or windows at the same time in meetings
summary: The briefing's rollout, default state, licensing and PowerShell controls are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. The existing screen-sharing policy's admin path is correct but stops one step before the setting.

claims.claim: No licensing requirement specific to simultaneous sharing is published at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams two presenters share screens simultaneously meeting licensing; Teams simultaneous screen sharing pricing license meter. Opened Manage Teams licenses, Teams service description and Teams Premium licensing; none specifies a simultaneous-sharing licence.

claims.claim: No meter specific to this simultaneous-sharing feature is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous screen sharing pricing license meter. Read Teams service description, Teams Premium licensing and Teams interoperability pricing excerpts; none names a meter for simultaneous sharing in built-in Teams clients.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how the second simultaneous stream appears on other clients such as mobile or Teams Rooms.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous two presenters screen sharing AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center license mobile Rooms; Teams simultaneous sharing mobile. Read roadmap, MC1528014, content-sharing policy and returned client excerpts; no second-stream client behaviour found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no Teams admin center path for the multiple-screenshare setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams multiple screenshare admin center; Teams Multiple VBSS MultiVBSS meeting options admin center simultaneous screen sharing; AllowMultipleScreenshare. Opened content-sharing policy and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; neither gives that UI path.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMultipleScreenshare $false is a documented MicrosoftTeams PowerShell call, subject to the stated no-effect caveat.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy
    [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>]
    [-AllowMultipleScreenshare <Boolean>]
$false: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.

claims.claim: AllowMultipleScreenshare controls Multiple Screenshare for the tenant or a particular user through meeting policies.
claims.quote: This setting enables Tenant Admins to turn on the Multiple Screenshare feature. It controls whether Multiple Screenshare is on or off for the entire tenant or for a particular user.

claims.claim: The AllowMultipleScreenshare reference warns that the feature is not fully released and the setting currently has no effect.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The reference describes true as making Multiple VBSS meeting options available and enabled for the organiser.
claims.quote: $true: Multiple VBSS (MultiVBSS) meeting options are available and enabled for the organizer.

claims.claim: The reference describes false as hiding MultiVBSS meeting options from the organiser.
claims.quote: $false: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited reference does not explicitly identify AllowMultipleScreenshare as the control for MC1528014 or roadmap item 80239.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowMultipleScreenshare; Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy AllowMultipleScreenshare. Opened the full cmdlet reference and checked its parameter description and item identifiers; it describes Multiple Screenshare but does not cite MC1528014 or 80239.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing reaches the page section containing the existing screen-sharing control.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit. Go to the Content sharing section.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the repeated paths to 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing > Screen sharing mode' in Teams admin center. The cited content-sharing policy page names Screen sharing mode as the setting in that section.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ScreenSharingMode <value> configures the existing screen-sharing mode.
claims.quote:
You can also use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet to control the content sharing settings. Set the following parameters:
- ScreenSharingMode

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].scope; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Screen sharing mode is a per-user policy governing whether a user can share a desktop or window in a Teams meeting.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy. The setting controls whether a user can share a desktop and window in a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: Screen sharing mode governs each user's sharing permissions rather than the number of simultaneous presenters.
claims.quote: Set this to SingleApplication to allow the user to share an application at a given point in time. Set this to EntireScreen to allow the user to share anything on their screens. Set this to Disabled to prohibit the user from sharing their screens.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated feature page describing this two-presenter rollout beyond the cited parameter reference.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams two presenters; Teams simultaneous two presenters screen sharing AllowMultipleScreenshare; Teams Multiple VBSS MultiVBSS meeting options. Opened content-sharing policy and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no dedicated rollout feature page found.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not name a specific administrator role for its tenant-level control.

claims.claim: The supplied notice gives no location for the tenant-level control.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1528014 in full for control location, portal navigation and commands; it announces tenant-level admin control without specifying a location.
